docs.title: Vitrify
docs.text:
vitrify turns a mutable SPARQL response into a durable, inspectable local file with its query and retrieval evidence.

  • SPARQL endpoint

    Send the exact query to Wikidata's mutable endpoint.

    https://query.wikidata.org/sparql

  • Vitrify command

    Capture EU-capital labels in a local RO-Crate.

    printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?label
WHERE {
  ?country wdt:P463 wd:Q458 ;
           wdt:P36 ?capital .
  ?capital rdfs:label ?label .
  FILTER(LANG(?label) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?label
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://query.wikidata.org/sparql \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to eu-capitals

  • RO-Crate directory

    The ordinary response file is kept with the exact query and RO-Crate evidence.

    eu-capitals/ ├── results.csv ├── ro-crate-metadata.json └── query.rq

docs.title: Inspect the capture
What is vitrification?
docs.text: To vitrify is to turn something into glass. See also: Stanislaw Lem Fiasco.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
cargo install vitrify

See Installation for the Rust version this command needs.

docs.title: Add an example
docs.text:
Add a Markdown page under docs/examples/. Its frontmatter supplies the SPARQL query, the endpoint URL, and an optional requested format:

---
"@context": urn:vitrify:examples
endpoints:
  - https://query.wikidata.org/sparql
format: csv
query: |
  PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
  PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>

  SELECT ?person WHERE {
    ?person wdt:P31 wd:Q5 .
  }
  LIMIT 5
---

# Five humans

Retrieve five items classified as humans.

Use a descriptive filename and one level-one heading. Keep the query complete. The result preview shows the first five rows. Omit format to let the endpoint choose its response type. The vitrify sparql command lists accepted format names.

A context example records a remote JSON-LD context instead of a SPARQL query:

---
"@context": urn:vitrify:examples
context: https://www.w3.org/ns/anno.jsonld
---

# Web Annotation

Open a pull request that includes the new page.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
vitrify is a Cargo package. Install Rust 1.88 or newer, then install the package from crates.io:

cargo install vitrify

Cargo puts the vitrify command on PATH. This prints the installed version:

vitrify --version

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: This page describes capabilities being considered for Vitrify. They are planned work, not features of the current CLI, and no delivery dates are set.

docs.title: Planned capabilities
docs.text:
• More retrieval types: retrieve a linked-data representation for an IRI and fetch an arbitrary URL as a local file.
  • Croissant metadata: listed on Outputs.
  • Additional representations: offer optional raw-response or normalized graph outputs for workflows that need them.

See vitrify sparql and vitrify context for the current commands, and the RO-Crate output guide for the files vitrify sparql writes.

docs.title: vitrify sparql
docs.text:
vitrify sparql sends one query to a SPARQL endpoint and saves the response body in an output directory.

vitrify sparql \
  --endpoint https://query.wikidata.org/sparql \
  --query docs/examples/female-persons/query.rq \
  --format csv \
  --to female-persons

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
Argument Required Description --endpoint IRI SPARQL endpoint URL. --query PATH or --query - Read the query from a UTF-8 file, or read standard input when the value is -. --to DIRECTORY Directory for the result and its RO-Crate files. --format FORMAT Request a response format; also supplies a fallback filename extension.

The query must not be empty. Standard input is read only when --query - is specified. Vitrify saves the query text it sends as query.rq in the output directory.

docs.title: Formats
docs.text:
--format Requested media type Fallback extension json application/sparql-results+json .json xml application/sparql-results+xml .xml csv text/csv .csv tsv text/tab-separated-values .tsv turtle text/turtle .ttl ntriples application/n-triples .nt rdfxml application/rdf+xml .rdf jsonld application/ld+json .jsonld

Vitrify chooses the filename extension from the response Content-Type, even when it differs from --format. If that media type is missing or unrecognized, it uses the extension for --format. With neither available, it writes results.dat and prints a warning.

When --format is omitted, Vitrify does not send an Accept header.

Vitrify saves successful response bytes unchanged. The requested format does not guarantee the endpoint returns that media type; use the recorded Content-Type to identify the response.

A non-success HTTP response returns a nonzero exit status and saves the failed retrieval in the RO-Crate metadata, including its error and duration.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
Argument Required Description URL Absolute HTTP(S) URL of the context. --as jsonld or --as yamlld Serialization of the printed document. jsonld is the default.

A failed fetch, a non-success status, or a body that is not a context returns a nonzero exit status and prints nothing to standard output.

The document keeps the fetched @context unchanged and has no @id. contentUrl is the final URL. The request records the URL that was asked for. Vitrify also records the byte size, SHA-256 of the downloaded bytes, media type, response headers, and the time of the retrieval. Metadata keys are absolute IRIs. Literals are JSON-LD value objects, so a term's type, language, and direction do not apply to them. A processor rejects the document when a context term maps one of those IRIs to a different IRI. @container on a term whose name is one of those IRIs applies to the literal. @list wraps it in an RDF list.

A remote @context URL or @import is not fetched again. Vitrify prints a warning on standard error and copies that reference as it is.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Each example shows a saved SPARQL query, a preview of its response, and the files Vitrify wrote. Open a file link in the directory preview to inspect the captured source, response, or RO-Crate metadata.

Query from a file is probably the most production-ready approach: the query can be versioned and reused in a pipeline. The other examples use printf and standard input to keep their commands self-contained.

  • Female Nobel laureates

  • Fourth-order classes

  • Metaclasses by instance count

  • Metaclasses of metaclasses

  • SELECT with Turtle requested

  • Third-order classes

  • Time-bounded subclasses

  • Query from a file

docs.text:

docs.title: Female Nobel laureates
docs.text:
This query returns female Nobel laureates from Wikidata across all prize categories, including Economic Sciences, with laureate labels, prize labels, and prize years, ordered from newest to oldest.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX p: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/>
PREFIX ps: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/statement/>
PREFIX pq: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/qualifier/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?person ?personLabel ?prizeLabel ?year WHERE {
  {
    SELECT DISTINCT ?prize WHERE {
      { ?prize wdt:P279* wd:Q7191 . } # Nobel Prize
      UNION
      { BIND(wd:Q47170 AS ?prize) } # Economic Sciences
    }
  }
  ?person p:P166 [
    ps:P166 ?prize ;
    pq:P585 ?awardDate

    wdt:P21 wd:Q6581072 . # sex or gender: female
  BIND(YEAR(?awardDate) AS ?year)
  ?person rdfs:label ?personLabel .
  FILTER(LANG(?personLabel) = "en")
  ?prize rdfs:label ?prizeLabel .
  FILTER(LANG(?prizeLabel) = "en")
}
ORDER BY DESC(?year) ?person
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \

docs.title: Fourth-order classes
docs.text:
The query lists all items in Wikidata whose recorded instance of (P31) type is fourth-order class or a subclass of that type, ordered by English label and item URI. A fourth-order class has third-order classes as its instances. This query selects recorded types; it does not check the order of every instance.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT DISTINCT ?class ?classLabel WHERE {
  ?class wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q24027474 .
  OPTIONAL {
    ?class rdfs:label ?englishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?englishLabel) = "en")
  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?englishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?class), "entity/")) AS ?classLabel)
}
ORDER BY ?classLabel ?class
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format csv \

docs.title: Metaclasses of metaclasses
docs.text:
The query finds explicitly typed metaclasses in Wikidata whose recorded direct instances are all explicitly typed metaclasses too. It requires at least one instance, ranks matches by distinct instance count, and shows one example instance per match. Metaclass typing uses instance of (P31), followed by the type's subclass of (P279) hierarchy to metaclass.

Wikidata calls a class of second-order classes a third-order class. The query also allows mixed or higher orders. It checks recorded truthy P31 values; missing metaclass typing excludes a candidate, and unrecorded instances cannot be checked. Ties and example instances are selected by URI.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?metaclass ?metaclassLabel ?instanceCount ?exampleInstance ?exampleInstanceLabel WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?metaclass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?instance) AS ?instanceCount)
           (MIN(STR(?instance)) AS ?exampleInstanceIRI) WHERE {
      {
        SELECT DISTINCT ?metaclass WHERE {
          ?metaclass wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q19478619 .
        }
      }
      ?instance wdt:P31 ?metaclass .
      FILTER NOT EXISTS {
        ?counterexample wdt:P31 ?metaclass .
        FILTER NOT EXISTS {
          ?counterexample wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q19478619 .
        }
      }
    }
    GROUP BY ?metaclass
    ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
  }
  BIND(IRI(?exampleInstanceIRI) AS ?exampleInstance)
  OPTIONAL {
    ?metaclass rdfs:label ?englishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?englishLabel) = "en")
  }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?exampleInstance rdfs:label ?exampleEnglishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?exampleEnglishLabel) = "en")
  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?englishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?metaclass), "entity/")) AS ?metaclassLabel)
  BIND(COALESCE(?exampleEnglishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?exampleInstance), "entity/")) AS ?exampleInstanceLabel)
}
ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to metaclasses-of-metaclasses

docs.title: Save as query.rq
docs.text:
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?label
WHERE {
  ?country wdt:P463 wd:Q458 ;
           wdt:P36 ?capital .
  ?capital rdfs:label ?label .
  FILTER(LANG(?label) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?label

docs.title: Run the query
docs.text:
vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query query.rq \
  --format csv \
  --to eu-capitals

This runs the same query as EU capitals.

docs.title: SELECT with Turtle requested
docs.text:
This example requests Turtle for a SELECT query. The endpoint may return another response format or reject the request. Vitrify records the actual response type and chooses the filename extension from it — for example results.xml or results.json — falling back to .ttl only if that media type is missing or unrecognized. Older history entries still use results.ttl from before that naming rule.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?person ?personName WHERE {
  ?person rdfs:label ?personName .
  FILTER(LANG(?personName) = "en")
}
LIMIT 5
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format turtle \
  --to select-turtle

docs.title: Third-order classes
docs.text:
The query lists all items in Wikidata whose recorded instance of (P31) type is third-order class or a subclass of that type, ordered by English label and item URI. A third-order class has second-order classes as its instances. This query selects recorded types; it does not check the order of every instance.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT DISTINCT ?class ?classLabel WHERE {
  ?class wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q24017465 .
  OPTIONAL {
    ?class rdfs:label ?englishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?englishLabel) = "en")
  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?englishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?class), "entity/")) AS ?classLabel)
}
ORDER BY ?classLabel ?class
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to third-order-classes

docs.title: Time-bounded subclasses
docs.text:
This Wikidata query finds subclass statements with start and end qualifiers, then returns their English labels as SPARQL Results JSON.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX p: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/>
PREFIX ps: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/statement/>
PREFIX pq: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/qualifier/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?subclass ?subclassName ?superclass ?superclassName ?start ?end WHERE {
  ?subclass p:P279 ?subclassStatement .
  ?subclassStatement ps:P279 ?superclass ;
                     pq:P580 ?start ;
                     pq:P582 ?end .

  FILTER NOT EXISTS {
    ?subclass wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q22938576 .   # not a race (competition)
  }

  FILTER NOT EXISTS {
    ?subclass wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q3139516 .  # not an abbot or other church official
  }

  ?subclass rdfs:label ?subclassName .
  ?superclass rdfs:label ?superclassName .
  FILTER(LANG(?subclassName) = "en")
  FILTER(LANG(?superclassName) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?subclassName ?start ?end
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format json \
  --to time-bounded-subclasses

docs.title: Metaclasses by instance count
docs.text:
The query ranks metaclasses in Wikidata by their number of distinct direct instance of (P31) statements. Candidates are explicitly typed metaclasses: they have an instance of type equal to metaclass or one of its subclasses, such as second-order class. This follows recorded types, rather than checking that each instance is itself a class. The counts use truthy P31 values and do not include instances inherited through subclasses. Ties are resolved by item URI.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?metaclass ?metaclassLabel ?instanceCount WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?metaclass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?instance) AS ?instanceCount) WHERE {
      {
        SELECT DISTINCT ?metaclass WHERE {
          ?metaclass wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q19478619 .
        }
      }
      ?instance wdt:P31 ?metaclass .
    }
    GROUP BY ?metaclass
    ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
  }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?metaclass rdfs:label ?englishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?englishLabel) = "en")
  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?englishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?metaclass), "entity/")) AS ?metaclassLabel)
}
ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to top-metaclasses

docs.title: RO-Crate
docs.text:
vitrify sparql --to DIRECTORY writes the result and two evidence files into the directory:

female-persons/
  query.rq
  results.csv
  ro-crate-metadata.json

The result file name follows the format rules.

query.rq contains the exact query text sent to the endpoint. It is included even when the query was read from standard input.

ro-crate-metadata.json is an RO-Crate 1.3 JSON-LD document describing the retrieval. It links the result and query files and records their byte sizes and SHA-256 checksums, the result media type when provided, the endpoint, response status, final URL, requested Accept value when one was sent, and retrieval times. The retrieval action has a completed or failed status. Linked PropertyValue entities record retrieval duration in seconds. Duration covers the request, redirects, and response download; it excludes final metadata writing.

The root dataset's license text says that Vitrify does not assert a license for retrieved data. Check the source endpoint's terms before reusing that data.

Open the complete example metadata file:

RO-Crate metadata for the Wikidata example

docs.title: Reusing an output directory
docs.text:
A successful retrieval into an existing directory overwrites query.rq, the result file with the selected extension, and ro-crate-metadata.json. Result files with other extensions remain: receiving JSON after a previous CSV response leaves both results.json and results.csv, while the new metadata describes only results.json. Use a new directory or preserve the existing capture in version control before retrieving again.

Vitrify initializes the query and metadata before requesting the endpoint. It replaces the metadata atomically when the retrieval finishes. A network or HTTP failure records the error and duration and returns a nonzero exit status. A streaming failure can leave a partial response, identified as incomplete in the metadata rather than linked as a successful result. An interrupted process can leave an active action; treat that capture as incomplete.

Invalid inputs fail before retrieval initialization. If the output directory cannot be written, the CLI reports the filesystem error; a saved attempt may not be available.

docs.title: Example history
docs.text: Each example has WDQS and QLever tabs, each with its own command, saved files, and response-size history. Select a bar to open that attempt's permanent page. The newest attempt is selected by default, including failures. Hover or focus a bar for its timestamp, outcome, byte count, and duration. A hollow ? marker indicates an unavailable size; bar height represents the saved response size in bytes. Duration appears beneath each bar. Older captures use estimated durations derived from their recorded timestamps, marked with ≈.

docs.title: EU capitals
docs.text:
This Wikidata query returns EU-capital labels in English.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?label
WHERE {
  ?country wdt:P463 wd:Q458 ;
           wdt:P36 ?capital .
  ?capital rdfs:label ?label .
  FILTER(LANG(?label) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?label
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to eu-capitals

This Wikidata query returns EU-capital labels in English.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?label
WHERE {
  ?country wdt:P463 wd:Q458 ;
           wdt:P36 ?capital .
  ?capital rdfs:label ?label .
  FILTER(LANG(?label) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?label
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://query.wikidata.org/sparql \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to eu-capitals

docs.title: Female Nobel laureates
docs.text:
This query returns female Nobel laureates from Wikidata across all prize categories, including Economic Sciences, with laureate labels, prize labels, and prize years, ordered from newest to oldest.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX p: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/>
PREFIX ps: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/statement/>
PREFIX pq: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/qualifier/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?person ?personLabel ?prizeLabel ?year WHERE {
  {
    SELECT DISTINCT ?prize WHERE {
      { ?prize wdt:P279* wd:Q7191 . } # Nobel Prize
      UNION
      { BIND(wd:Q47170 AS ?prize) } # Economic Sciences
    }
  }
  ?person p:P166 [
    ps:P166 ?prize ;
    pq:P585 ?awardDate
  ] ;
    wdt:P21 wd:Q6581072 . # sex or gender: female
  BIND(YEAR(?awardDate) AS ?year)
  ?person rdfs:label ?personLabel .
  FILTER(LANG(?personLabel) = "en")
  ?prize rdfs:label ?prizeLabel .
  FILTER(LANG(?prizeLabel) = "en")
}
ORDER BY DESC(?year) ?person
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to female-persons

PREFIX ps: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/statement/>
PREFIX pq: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/qualifier/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?person ?personLabel ?prizeLabel ?year WHERE {

    SELECT DISTINCT ?prize WHERE {
      { ?prize wdt:P279* wd:Q7191 . } # Nobel Prize

  ?person rdfs:label ?personLabel .
  FILTER(LANG(?personLabel) = "en")

  FILTER(LANG(?prizeLabel) = "en")
}
ORDER BY DESC(?year) ?person

docs.title: Fourth-order classes
docs.text:
The query lists all items in Wikidata whose recorded instance of (P31) type is fourth-order class or a subclass of that type, ordered by English label and item URI. A fourth-order class has third-order classes as its instances. This query selects recorded types; it does not check the order of every instance.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT DISTINCT ?class ?classLabel WHERE {
  ?class wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q24027474 .
  OPTIONAL {
    ?class rdfs:label ?englishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?englishLabel) = "en")
  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?englishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?class), "entity/")) AS ?classLabel)
}
ORDER BY ?classLabel ?class
' |

The query ranks metaclasses in Wikidata by their number of distinct direct instance of (P31) statements. Candidates are explicitly typed metaclasses: they have an instance of type equal to metaclass or one of its subclasses, such as second-order class. This follows recorded types, rather than checking that each instance is itself a class. The counts use truthy P31 values and do not include instances inherited through subclasses. Ties are resolved by item URI.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?metaclass ?metaclassLabel ?instanceCount WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?metaclass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?instance) AS ?instanceCount) WHERE {
      {
        SELECT DISTINCT ?metaclass WHERE {
          ?metaclass wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q19478619 .
        }
      }
      ?instance wdt:P31 ?metaclass .
    }
    GROUP BY ?metaclass
    ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
  }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?metaclass rdfs:label ?englishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?englishLabel) = "en")
  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?englishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?metaclass), "entity/")) AS ?metaclassLabel)
}
ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to top-metaclasses

PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?metaclass ?metaclassLabel ?instanceCount WHERE {

    SELECT ?metaclass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?instance) AS ?instanceCount) WHERE {

        SELECT DISTINCT ?metaclass WHERE {
          ?metaclass wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q19478619 .

      }
      ?instance wdt:P31 ?metaclass .
    }
    GROUP BY ?metaclass

    ?metaclass rdfs:label ?englishLabel .

  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?englishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?metaclass), "entity/")) AS ?metaclassLabel)
}
ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass

Candidates are explicitly typed metaclasses: they have an instance of type equal to metaclass or one of its subclasses, such as second-order class. This follows recorded types, rather than checking that each instance is itself a class. The counts use truthy P31 values and do not include instances inherited through subclasses. Ties are resolved by item URI.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?metaclass ?metaclassLabel ?instanceCount WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?metaclass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?instance) AS ?instanceCount) WHERE {
      {
        SELECT DISTINCT ?metaclass WHERE {
          ?metaclass wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q19478619 .
        }
      }
      ?instance wdt:P31 ?metaclass .
    }
    GROUP BY ?metaclass
    ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
    LIMIT 10
  }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?metaclass rdfs:label ?englishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?englishLabel) = "en")
  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?englishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?metaclass), "entity/")) AS ?metaclassLabel)
}
ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to top-metaclasses

SELECT ?metaclass ?metaclassLabel ?instanceCount ?exampleInstance ?exampleInstanceLabel WHERE {

      }
    }

    ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass

It requires at least one instance, ranks matches by distinct instance count, and shows one example instance per match. Metaclass typing uses instance of (P31), followed by the type's subclass of (P279) hierarchy to metaclass.

Wikidata calls a class of second-order classes a third-order class. The query also allows mixed or higher orders. It checks recorded truthy P31 values; missing metaclass typing excludes a candidate, and unrecorded instances cannot be checked. Ties and example instances are selected by URI.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?metaclass ?metaclassLabel ?instanceCount ?exampleInstance ?exampleInstanceLabel WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?metaclass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?instance) AS ?instanceCount)
           (MIN(STR(?instance)) AS ?exampleInstanceIRI) WHERE {
      {
        SELECT DISTINCT ?metaclass WHERE {
          ?metaclass wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q19478619 .
        }
      }
      ?instance wdt:P31 ?metaclass .
      FILTER NOT EXISTS {
        ?counterexample wdt:P31 ?metaclass .
        FILTER NOT EXISTS {
          ?counterexample wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q19478619 .
        }
      }
    }
    GROUP BY ?metaclass
    ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
  }
  BIND(IRI(?exampleInstanceIRI) AS ?exampleInstance)
  OPTIONAL {
    ?metaclass rdfs:label ?englishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?englishLabel) = "en")
  }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?exampleInstance rdfs:label ?exampleEnglishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?exampleEnglishLabel) = "en")
  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?englishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?metaclass), "entity/")) AS ?metaclassLabel)
  BIND(COALESCE(?exampleEnglishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?exampleInstance), "entity/")) AS ?exampleInstanceLabel)
}
ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://query.wikidata.org/sparql \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to metaclasses-of-metaclasses

docs.title: Metaclasses of metaclasses
docs.text:
The query finds explicitly typed metaclasses in Wikidata whose recorded direct instances are all explicitly typed metaclasses too. It requires at least one instance, ranks matches by distinct instance count, and shows one example instance per match. Metaclass typing uses instance of (P31), followed by the type's subclass of (P279) hierarchy to metaclass.

Wikidata calls a class of second-order classes a third-order class. The query also allows mixed or higher orders. It checks recorded truthy P31 values; missing metaclass typing excludes a candidate, and unrecorded instances cannot be checked. Ties and example instances are selected by URI.

        ?counterexample wdt:P31 ?metaclass .
        FILTER NOT EXISTS {
          ?counterexample wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q19478619 .
        }
      }
    }
    GROUP BY ?metaclass
    ORDER BY DESC(?instanceCount) ?metaclass
  }
  BIND(IRI(?exampleInstanceIRI) AS ?exampleInstance)
  OPTIONAL {
    ?metaclass rdfs:label ?englishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?englishLabel) = "en")

docs.title: Third-order classes
docs.text:
The query lists all items in Wikidata whose recorded instance of (P31) type is third-order class or a subclass of that type, ordered by English label and item URI. A third-order class has second-order classes as its instances. This query selects recorded types; it does not check the order of every instance.

printf '%s' 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT DISTINCT ?class ?classLabel WHERE {
  ?class wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q24017465 .
  OPTIONAL {
    ?class rdfs:label ?englishLabel .
    FILTER(LANG(?englishLabel) = "en")
  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?englishLabel, STRAFTER(STR(?class), "entity/")) AS ?classLabel)
}
ORDER BY ?classLabel ?class
' |
  vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query - \
  --format csv \

docs.title: Save as query.rq
docs.text:
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?label
WHERE {
  ?country wdt:P463 wd:Q458 ;
           wdt:P36 ?capital .
  ?capital rdfs:label ?label .
  FILTER(LANG(?label) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?label

docs.title: Run the query
docs.text:
vitrify sparql --endpoint https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata \
  --query query.rq \
  --format csv \
  --to eu-capitals

This runs the same query as EU capitals.
